newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar closes softer in moderate trading.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar closes softer in moderate trading.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar closed weaker on Friday at C$1.3641 (US$0.7331) from Thursday's close at C$1.3620 (US$0.7343) in moderate trading, dealers said.
* They said a corporate interest to buy U.S. dollars weakened the Canadian currency, and the move past C$1.3625 (US$0.7340) triggered heavy stop-loss selling of the currency.
The index rose 0.2 percent in the month and 2.2 percent in the year to 137.1, Statistics Canada said Friday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unadjusted CPI to rise 0.25 percent on the month. The survey also forecast a 2.2 percent year-over-year rise.

The Canadian dollar has followed a weakening trend during the month of February mainly on selling against the Australian dollar and the Japanese yen, Farrill said. He said he expects the currency to weaken again heading into Monday trading.
"We anticipate more selling of the Canadian dollar versus the Aussie dollar and the yen," he said.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar climbed to 1.2380 marks from Thursday's close of 1.2367 marks and rose to 90.23 yen from 89.88 yen.
